Empirical Research Plan  
“Highways, Trade Costs, and the Spatial Dispersion of Economic Activity inside China”

------------------------------------------------------------
1. Identification Strategy  
Choice: Difference-in-Differences (two–way fixed effects) complemented by an event-study.  

Why it fits  
• The highway network rolled out in clearly dated phases (pre-1997, 1997–2003, post-2003).  
• Many peripheral counties were “accidentally” connected because planners only optimised inter-city links between large metropolitan endpoints. Conditional on lying on a feasible corridor, whether a given county was reached in the 1997–2003 tranche or not is plausibly exogenous to its own economic trend.  
• We have panel data with one clean pre-period (1990 or 1997) and one post-period (2006) plus an earlier baseline that can be used to check pre-trends.  
• A DID allows intuitive interpretation of a treatment that is binary (“gained an NTHS link 1997-2003”) and staggered (some counties connected earlier, some later, some never).  
• The event-study version lets us visualise and test the parallel-trends assumption.

------------------------------------------------------------
2. Treatment and Control  

Treatment variable  
Treated county = 1 if:  
a) No NTHS link within 10 km of the county centroid as of 1997, and  
b) At least one NTHS segment within 10 km completed between 1997 and 2003 that reduces shortest-time driving distance to the nearest metropolitan “hub” by ≥20 %.  
(Results are robust to 5 km / 15 km radii and 10 % / 30 % distance cut-offs.)

Control group  
Counties satisfying a) but not b); i.e., they still lacked an NTHS link by 2006. To improve comparability, we restrict both groups to counties that lie inside a 50-km “feasible corridor band” around the pre-announced least-cost path connecting consecutive metropolitan endpoints.  

Treatment timing  
Treat = 0 in 1990 and 1997, = 1 from 2003 onward for counties connected 1997-2003; never = 0 for pure controls. Counties connected only after 2003 are dropped from the baseline DID but used in robustness tests/event studies (staggered cohorts).

------------------------------------------------------------
3. Key Identifying Assumptions  

A1. Parallel trends: Absent an NTHS connection, treated and control counties would have experienced the same growth trajectory 1997-2006.  
Plausibility: Pre-period data (1990-1997) permit a direct test. Visual inspection of event-study coefficients should show no significant pre-trend.  

A2. As-good-as-random route placement within corridors: Conditional on endpoints, topo-graphic constraints, and corridor band fixed effects, the exact counties chosen for the 1997-2003 tranche are unrelated to their idiosyncratic future growth shocks.  
Plausibility: Central planning focused on technical cost (terrain, bridges, tunnels) and political visibility, not county-level GDP. We can proxy technical cost with slope and river crossings to show that adding these variables does not move the treatment coefficient.  

A3. No anticipation between 1990-1997: County economic agents did not change location decisions in advance of construction.  
Plausibility: Provincial highway bureaus could not credibly announce precise routes until late 1996, while actual construction accelerated only after 1998. Event-study should show flat coefficients pre-1997.  

A4. Stable unit treatment value (limited spillovers within 50 km band): Economic effects in a treated county do not mechanically contaminate the control group inside the same band.  
Plausibility: The corridor restriction lowers the chance that shocks spill far enough to reach pure controls; robustness checks that drop neighbouring controls will be run.

------------------------------------------------------------
4. Main Threats and Mitigation  

T1. Endogenous route selection (rich or fast-growing counties lobbied for earlier junctions).  
Mitigation:  
• Add county-level 1990 controls (log GDP, population, industrial share).  
• Instrument actual connection with “straight-line shortest path between endpoints × geophysical least-cost surface” indicator (planned route, not final built) in 2SLS.  
• Placebo test using pre-1990 growth (1982-1990, from census) as outcome.  

T2. Spillovers/general-equilibrium effects (treated counties grow at expense of nearby controls).  
Mitigation:  
• Cluster standard errors at the prefecture (labour-market) level.  
• Run spatial lag models to test whether excluding controls within 30 km of a treated county changes results.  
• Report both “overall” and “net of neighbours” estimates.  

T3. Measurement error in highway completion dates or county boundaries.  
Mitigation:  
• Cross-validate ACASIAN route dates with Ministry of Transport yearbooks for a 10 % random sample.  
• Use 1999 boundary shapefile for all years (historically harmonised) to avoid “boundary drift.”  
• Show robustness to alternative 5 km vs. 15 km buffers.

------------------------------------------------------------
5. R Code Outline (executable)  

```r
#----------------------------------------------
# 0. Packages
library(data.table)
library(sf)        # spatial joins
library(fixest)    # fast TWFE and event-study
library(ggplot2)

#----------------------------------------------
# 1. Load data
cnty   <- fread("china_county_panel.csv")          # socioeconomic data 1990, 1997, 2006
roads  <- st_read("nths_segments.shp")             # geo-coded, with completion_year
bounds <- st_read("county_1999_boundaries.shp")    # harmonised county shapes

#----------------------------------------------
# 2. Build treatment variable
#   a) attach earliest NTHS distance by year
segments_9797 <- roads[roads$completion_year <= 1997, ]
segments_9703 <- roads[roads$completion_year %between% c(1998,2003), ]

# Distance of centroid to nearest segment in each phase
cnty_sf <- merge(bounds, cnty, by = "county_id")

cnty_sf$dist97 <- st_distance(st_centroid(cnty_sf), segments_9797) |> apply(1,min)
cnty_sf$dist03 <- st_distance(st_centroid(cnty_sf), segments_9703) |> apply(1,min)

# Treated if dist97>10000 & dist03<=10000 (10 km radius)
cnty_sf[, treated := as.integer(dist97>10000 & dist03<=10000)]

#----------------------------------------------
# 3. Collapse to wide for DID 1997–2006
d97 <- cnty_sf[year==1997, .(county_id, log_gdp97 = log(gdp), treated)]
d06 <- cnty_sf[year==2006, .(county_id, log_gdp06 = log(gdp))]

d_w  <- merge(d97, d06)
d_w[, dl_gdp := log_gdp06 - log_gdp97]

# Controls from 1990 base year
ctrl <- cnty_sf[year==1990, .(county_id,
                              log_pop90 = log(pop),
                              ind_sh90  = ind_emp/emp_tot,
                              slope     = mean_slope)]
d_w  <- merge(d_w, ctrl)

#----------------------------------------------
# 4. Main DID specification
did_spec <- feols(dl_gdp ~ treated + log_pop90 + ind_sh90 + slope | province, 
                  data = d_w, cluster = ~prefecture)

summary(did_spec)

#----------------------------------------------
# 5. Event-study using Sun & Abraham (staggered)
# reshape to long, keep 1990, 1997, 2006
long <- cnty_sf[year %in% c(1990,1997,2006)]
long[, treat_year := ifelse(treated==1, 2003, 0)]  # cohort year 0 for never-treated

es <- feols(log(gdp) ~ sunab(treat_year, year) + log_pop90 + ind_sh90 + slope |
              county_id + year,
            data = long, cluster = ~prefecture)
iplot(es) + geom_vline(xintercept=0, lty=2)

#----------------------------------------------
# 6. Robustness: drop controls within 30 km of treatment
neighbor <- st_is_within_distance(st_centroid(cnty_sf[treated==1,]), 
                                  st_centroid(cnty_sf), dist = 30000)
drop_ids <- unique(unlist(neighbor))
d_rb <- d_w[!(county_id %in% drop_ids & treated==0)]
feols(dl_gdp ~ treated + log_pop90 + ind_sh90 | province, 
      data = d_rb, cluster = ~prefecture)
```

------------------------------------------------------------
6. Expected Results  

Economic theory (new economic geography with trade-cost reductions between asymmetric markets) offers two competing mechanisms:  
• Centripetal: Agglomeration economies in large metros may intensify, draining activity from periphery.  
• Centrifugal: Lower trade costs allow firms to relocate to cheaper land/labour in the periphery while keeping access to metro markets.  

Because the treated counties are small and had a 1:25 GDP gap initially, I expect a modest but positive growth effect: roughly +6 % (≈ 0.06 log-points) higher GDP growth 1997-2006 relative to comparable controls, driven primarily by industrial GVA (+10 %); agricultural GVA likely falls slightly (−2 %) and services little changed. Urban population share should rise by 1–1.5 p.p.

------------------------------------------------------------
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (DID)  

C1: Parallel pre-trends verified (event-study) ............... 1  
C2: No anticipation (flat coefficients before t = 0) .......... 0.8  
C3: Exogenous treatment within corridor (balance tests) ....... 0.7  
C4: No interference/spillovers across units ................... 0.5  
C5: Stable composition (no county splits/mergers) ............. 1  

Overall: 4.0 / 5.
